body.p: Two old men. Once upon a time there were two old men, one Khanty, the other Nenets. Both of them had children. One was in the lower part of the sandy spit, the other was in the upper part, lived [there]. Their children played together, because the distance between the tents was small. Once the children say: "Let's make our fathers swear. Let's look at their shamanism: are they shamans at all. The kids went up the upper shore. They say to the father: "Father, the one who lives in the lower reaches of the shore considers himself stronger, get ready." And those who live in the lower reaches of the shore said to their father: "Father, your friend, who lives in the upper reaches of the shore, wants to measure his strength with you, get ready. We have warned you to get ready." The old men thought for the rest of the day. And then one old man said: "Tomorrow go to the shore to watch how we will measure our strength." The next day came. The children went to the shore. Meanwhile, from the upper reaches, a huge stag came running, ran with a croak. A goat came to this croaking: its horns are in the middle of the forehead, the ends are bent down with a hook. They immediately bumped their horns together, throughout the day they measure their strength, swear, fight. At the end of the day, a deer with branched horns fell to the ground. The crooked one stuck his horn in his neck. The children got scared. The crooked-horned stag remained. It got dark, and the old man, who lived in the upper reaches, came home. The old man says: "I have grown old, I have not found a hole in the spinal cord. I would have killed him right away. Children, don't play with such force anymore. In six months I will go to other lands. In the spring I will not be, he has greatly pierced my soul. The next day, children from the neighboring tent came and said: "Our father is no more, he went to the land of the beast."
